name: Willoughby Corner Phase IA Senior
headline: Willoughby Corner Phase IA Senior (now Búho Place) is a 63-home, all income-restricted, all-electric building for adults 55+ in east Lafayette, the first building of Boulder County Housing Authority's 400-home Willoughby Corner neighborhood; it won a 2022 Round One federal 9% award and began leasing in December 2024.
why_it_matters: It anchored a phased master plan in which a 9% senior building was paired with a 4%-bond family phase (Phase IB) to finance one 192-home first phase on city-bought land dedicated to permanent affordability.

status.label: Built and leasing/occupied (leasing from December 2024)
status.detail: Groundbreaking was 2023-07-19 and Phase 1 reached substantial completion on 2024-12-31. Lafayette announced leasing at Búho Place on 2024-12-10; BCHA reported 51 of 63 homes leased as of 2025-02-28, and the Phase 1 grand opening was 2025-08-21. No placed-in-service or 8609 record was found online.

next_step: Watch for CHFA placed-in-service or compliance records; the next phase (Phase 2A, 32 IDD homes) won 2026 credits.

key_numbers.meaning: About $13.5M over 10 years (Boulder County called it $13M); no state credit is shown on the award report.
All homes at or below 60% AMI.
For all 192 Phase 1 homes, community center and infrastructure ($83M hard costs).

background.text: Lafayette, Boulder County and BCHA bought the 24-acre industrial site at 120th and Emma in 2017; the intergovernmental agreement dedicates it to permanently affordable housing and requires at least 10% of affordable rentals to serve adults 55+.

BCHA planned the 9% senior building and a 4%-bond family phase (93 homes in the application; 129 in the Round Two award) together as one Phase 1, sharing infrastructure costs pro rata (63 of 400 homes, about $22,000 per home).
The tenant selection plan gives a preference to income-qualified households displaced by the December 2021 Marshall Fire.
Lafayette rezoned the site from M1 industrial to R4 high-density residential in April 2022 (unanimous Planning Commission and council votes); the final PUD was recorded on 2022-11-30.
Lafayette City Council unanimously approved the Phase 1 site plan on 2023-04-18; BCHA said the Phase 1 loans would close in early May 2023.
Pinkard reached substantial completion of all six Phase 1 buildings on 2024-12-31, about 15 months after starting, despite a five-month permitting delay.
Housing Choice Voucher holders can use vouchers at Willoughby Corner; the 30%, 40% and 50% AMI homes are reported fully leased.

discrepancies.text: Boulder County's 2022 release says the 24-acre site was bought for $3.5 million, while its April 2023 release refers to a $3.1 million land purchase.
The 2022 application said the companion family phase would have 93 homes, while CHFA's 2022 Round Two award report lists Phase IB with 129 homes.
